question: A 35-year-old man with no past medical history presents to his primary care physician with complaints of fatigue. He states that his life has been hectic lately and that everything seems to be falling apart. He is scared that he will lose his job, that his wife will leave him, and that his children will not be able to afford to go to college. His worries are severe enough that they have began to interfere with his daily activities. His wife is also present and states that he has a very secure job and that they are well off financially. She says that he has always worried about something since she met him years ago. What medication would benefit this patient long term?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic stress -> anxiety -> Escitalopram -> improved mood -> 80% CHAIN: Generalized anxiety disorder -> Escitalopram -> symptom relief -> 85% CHAIN: Chronic worry -> Escitalopram -> reduced anxiety symptoms -> 80%
enhanced_information: For a 35-year-old man with chronic worry and anxiety symptoms, Escitalopram is a suitable long-term medication option based on its efficacy in treating anxiety and improving mood. Evidence paths confirm Escitalopram's effectiveness in treating anxiety symptoms and overall mood improvement.
analysis: The patient presents with chronic worry and anxiety symptoms that are interfering with his daily life. Escitalopram, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), is a suitable long-term medication option for treating anxiety and improving mood in this case.
